description: Honest machine-readable + human-readable matrix mapping (language × build_system_id × test_framework_id) onto coverage status {backed | partial | missing | unknown}. Backed means an end-to-end deterministic verifier path is wired; partial means detection works but verifier path is incomplete; missing means the combination is a known target with no oracle wiring today; unknown is the explicit fail-closed default. Unsupported combinations NEVER silently become backed or partial.
purpose: Rung 3 of the post-audit Claude-lane sequence. Closes the 'what does verifier-governed actually mean' credibility gap identified in the gap-to-100 audit. Provides the truth layer for any future claim about language coverage and gives the next adapter expansion (Ruby/PHP/Swift/Kotlin/Scala/Elixir/.NET) a clear scope.

partial.reason: JavaGradleAdapter detects build.gradle.kts but compiles Java only (gradle compileJava, not compileKotlin)
Build oracle relies on package.json having a 'build' script — not a true tsc gate
Build oracle weak (same as jest path); vitest execution wired

honesty_rules: A row is BACKED only if a deterministic verifier/oracle is wired end-to-end: detection in BuildAdapter registry + shadow build + test execution + corpus/repair pipeline. Existence of a scripts/validators/ module is NOT sufficient (those are DATA ENGINE ONLY).

A row is PARTIAL when SOMETHING is wired but the path is incomplete: weak build oracle, missing repair path, partial language support in a generic adapter, or test framework recognized but not executed.
A row is MISSING when the combination is a known target but no deterministic verifier path exists in this repo today.
Any (lang, build, test) NOT in COVERAGE_MATRIX returns UNKNOWN via lookup(). There is no implicit fallback to PARTIAL or BACKED.
Every BuildAdapter's canonical (build_system_id, test_framework_id) MUST appear in the matrix — verified by test_every_adapter_static_output_is_covered.
Node refinement test framework ids (vitest, mocha) MUST appear in the matrix — verified by test_node_adapter_refinements_are_covered.
invariants: lookup(language, build_system_id, test_framework_id) returns a CoverageEntry with status BACKED, PARTIAL, MISSING, or UNKNOWN — never raises.
Unsupported combinations fail closed to UNKNOWN with a 'fails closed' note.
classify_for_build_test(build, test) agrees with lookup() for every matrix row.
to_markdown() output is byte-identical to docs/VERIFIER_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md (after \r\n normalization).
lookup() and to_markdown() never mutate signed evidence or any locks/sentinel/*.json file.
Corpus write guard remains active during tests (DETERMINEX_NO_CORPUS_WRITE=1 → CorpusWriteBlockedError).
No DETERMINEX_*/HF_HOME/OLLAMA_* env var is required to call lookup().
Safety defaults remain fail-closed after exercising the matrix.
BACKED rows' oracle_path mentions at least one wiring artifact (run_shadow_build, run_tests, RepairPipeline, or ShadowCompiler) — defensive check prevents empty claims.
remaining_gaps: Ruby/PHP/Swift/Scala/Elixir/.NET/CMake/Make adapters do not exist in BuildAdapterRegistry yet. The matrix documents them as MISSING; the adapter expansion is a follow-up rung.
TypeScript jest/vitest build oracle is weak (relies on package.json having a 'build' script). A real tsc gate would promote both to BACKED.
Kotlin/gradle/junit shows PARTIAL because JavaGradleAdapter compiles Java only. A KotlinGradleAdapter would promote it to BACKED.
C/C++ has NATIVE_C_CPP_REPAIR_LOCK_001 for the corpus side but no inference adapter; CMake/Make adapters would close this.
The matrix does not yet integrate with codebase_explorer.CodebaseExplorer.explore() output (no automatic 'coverage status' annotation in the WorkspaceReport). Targeted in a future rung.
Per-test-framework granularity is limited to the strings the registry exposes; multi-framework projects (e.g. jest + cypress) collapse to whichever the adapter picks first.
